question: What is strategic control? Explain its types.
sources: Strategic control framework: premise control, strategic surveillance, special alert control and implementation control

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Strategic control tracks a strategy while it is being carried out, checks whether its assumptions still hold, and makes changes where needed.
points.basis: Strategy evaluation: meaning of strategic control

points.label: Premise control
points.description: Systematically checks whether the assumptions (premises) on which the strategy is based are still valid.

points.label: Strategic surveillance
points.description: A broad, general watch on events inside and outside the firm that may affect the strategy.

points.label: Special alert control
points.description: A quick and thorough review of strategy when a sudden, unexpected event occurs, such as a natural disaster or a competitor's takeover.

points.label: Implementation control
points.description: Checks whether the steps and milestones of the strategy are achieved and whether the overall strategy needs to change.
